before.text: Reading an FR, TR, TEST or mapping through REST, the typed client or the REPL reports the creation and update times stored with that record. A read never reports the time of the read; when the store holds no time, the value is null (operator 2026-11-02: "This HAS to be fixed."; PR 87 slice P). A stored time written without an offset is read as UTC (operator 2026-11-02: "UTC"; pre-HV what-if finding: no contract row pinned it). A read never fills a missing date from the clock: a stored value without a complete date (a time alone, or a partial date) reads as null and is ignored when a mapping's creation time is chosen (operator 2026-11-02: "Strengthen 5 ACs, fix all 8 (Recommended)"; hostile validation finding R9-F4).

before.text: A test-owned temporary QBrain.AI instance uses the database inside its owned root: no inherited setting, in configuration or the process environment and in the canonical (QBrainAi, QBRAINAI_), legacy (Mcp, MCP_) or host-prefixed (DOTNET_, ASPNETCORE_) form, nor a connection-string or content-root variable, selects another database for it (a connection string, a data source, a database provider or an instance name), and a database selection outside the owned root is refused. Every consumer of a temporary instance takes its workspace, marker and server address from that instance, and no inherited setting overrides them. These are the unit-proved rules TR-MCP-NUKE-019 AC-6 relies on (operator 2026-10-29: "Strengthen ACs, fix both (Recommended)", "Run the 2 classes, AC first (Recommended)" and "Lane ACs (Recommended)"; operator 2026-10-30: "FR-MCP-TESTRESOURCE-001 (Recommended)"; hostile validation findings R8B-F2 and R8B-F3; holistic review findings PLAN-6, PLAN-7, RINT-1, RINT-2 and RINT-3). A REPL host started for a temporary instance names both a workspace and a marker, each strictly inside the instance's owned root, compared by path segment with either separator under the path's own syntax (a Windows-form path ignores case, drive letter included; a POSIX path compares ordinally; operator 2026-11-02: "Strengthen 5 ACs, fix all 8 (Recommended)", the sibling of hostile validation finding R9-F3) and with no '.' or '..' segment; the checkout's marker, another or sibling root, a parent-segment escape, the root itself as the marker, and a missing argument or value are refused (operator 2026-10-26: "if you surface new AC, add them without waiting for approval"; the start-argument rows of TemporaryInstanceChecksTests already prove it).

A unit test asserts no wall-clock bound (operator 2026-10-29: "Environment ACs (Recommended)"; holistic review findings MCPT-11, SVC-6 and MCPT-12). These rules are stated here once for TR-MCP-USECASE-019 AC-008 as well; the environment-delta rule moved to FR-MCP-047 ac-1 (operator 2026-10-29: "Move criteria that are misplaced.  Unit tests are for FR, Integration tests are for TR."). A unit test that checks a recorded time (an auth rotation, a selection or a session transition) takes the clock values from test-owned scripted inputs and asserts them exactly; it never compares with the current time, never sleeps to separate two times, and its result cannot change with elapsed time, scheduling delay or a change to the system clock (hostile validation round 10 finding R10-F3; strengthened between rounds under the operator's "Strengthening Acceptance Criteria should always be the recommended option" and "don't gate on me between rounds", 2026-11-03). This covers every recorded time a unit test checks, including the creation and update times a service stamps on a record it stores: the test supplies the service's clock as scripted times and asserts that each stamp equals the scripted time the service read (sibling sweep before round 11 of hostile validation round 10 finding R10-F3, 2026-11-03, under the same rulings). A wall-clock bound is an assertion whose outcome depends on how much real time passes: an elapsed time compared with a limit, or work the test expects to have happened during a short real-time wait (for example a periodic tick, a file-system event or a debounce); such a test is an integration test. A timeout whose only effect is to fail a test that would otherwise hang, set far above the time the awaited step needs, is not a wall-clock bound (holistic read before round 11, 2026-11-03, under the same rulings). A cancellation or timeout that a unit test arms on a real timer is such a wait when a step the test asserts must happen before the timer fires (finding of the hostile validation round 11 that stopped without a verdict, 2026-11-03, under the same rulings). Of the two sentences above, the hang-guard sentence governs: a timer a unit test arms whose only effect when it fires is to fail a test that would otherwise hang is a hang guard, not a wall-clock wait, even when an asserted step must finish before it fires. A test-armed cancellation or timeout is a wall-clock wait when its firing changes what the code under test does (for example it cancels or times out the operation whose outcome the test asserts) and an asserted step must happen before it fires. "Far above" means at least 100 times the longest real or scripted delay of the awaited step; a step with no real or scripted delay meets it for any positive timeout (holistic read before hostile validation round 12, finding B4; operator 2026-11-03: "Strengthen + margin (Recommended)"). The longest real or scripted delay of the awaited step is the sum of every real or scripted delay on its path: the waits, polls and delays the test scripts and the production waits, polls and deadlines the step passes through, read from the sources, never a measured run time (third holistic read before hostile validation round 12, finding d3; operator 2026-11-04: "Fix it", read as the recommended option "Strengthen + headroom"). A wait that happens only under a condition the step can meet, such as the 150 ms sleep before Microsoft.Data.Sqlite retries a statement that found the database busy, counts in that sum once for each poll on the path (fourth holistic read before hostile validation round 12, finding g1; operator 2026-11-04: "Strengthen: include them").
